title: NFL Jersey Quiz Part 2: Hard Mode
headline: NFL Jersey Quiz Part 2: Name The Team From A Tiny Piece Of Its Jersey
description: A hard NFL jersey quiz: eight tiny squares cut from current NFL jerseys, no numbers, no wordmarks, no logos. Just a stripe, a collar or a shoulder. Guess the team, reveal the answer, keep score.
intro: Every piece below is a small square cut from a current NFL jersey, about one sixtieth of the whole picture. No numbers, no wordmarks, no logo patches. What is left is the stuff fans stop noticing: a sleeve stripe, a collar, a shoulder panel.
Make your guess, then tap Show The Answer. Be honest and mark whether you got it, and your score adds up at the bottom.

items.piece: Gold, black and white stripes near the cuff of the black sleeve.
items.fact: Black and gold are the colors of Pittsburgh's city flag, and the Steelers took them on when the team was founded in 1933.

items.piece: The tip of a yellow horn curling over the royal blue shoulder.
items.fact: Rams halfback Fred Gehrke painted horns on the team's helmets in 1948, the first modern helmet emblem in pro football.

items.piece: White and gold stripes on the purple sleeve.
Silver, white and navy stripes at the end of the sleeve.
items.fact: Dallas usually wears white at home, a habit that goes back to the 1960s and general manager Tex Schramm.

items.piece: Wolf gray across the shoulder, with a sliver of action green at the edge.
items.fact: Seattle's wolf gray and action green look came from its 2012 redesign, the first season Nike made the NFL's uniforms.

items.piece: White stripes near the cuff of the green sleeve.
items.fact: The Jets' 2024 uniforms are based on the look they wore from the late 1970s through the 1980s.

items.piece: A gold lightning bolt over the powder blue shoulder.
items.fact: The Chargers wore powder blue in their first season, 1960, when they played in Los Angeles.

items.piece: White stripes on the scarlet sleeve.
items.fact: San Francisco began in 1946 in the All-America Football Conference and joined the NFL in 1950.
